vs Simplex/runtime assurance (sha2001simplicity, alshiekh2018shielding): Simplex and shielding require a *formally verified* safety controller and a model of the safety envelope (reachability/temporal-logic spec). Bouncer needs no such proof - microarchitectural safety is not a reachability invariant but a *relative performance floor*, so it only certifies that the learned controller's realized reward beats the fallback's, yielding a bounded-regret guarantee (Lemma) with no verified plant model.

vs constrained/safe-baseline RL (achiam2017cpo, laroche2019spibb, thomas2015hcpi): those methods enforce safety at *training time* against a known cost function or baseline dataset. Bouncer is a *runtime, off-policy* auditor wrapping an already-deployed black-box controller it did not train, enforcing the worst-case criterion online in hardware rather than at convergence.

vs set dueling (qureshi2007dip, jaleel2010rrip): Bouncer reuses the dedicated-sets-plus-counter substrate but repurposes it from policy *selection* to policy *trust* - it duels learned-vs-fallback to certify a competence advantage and feed a trust-gate FSM, not to pick an empirical winner; classic dueling assumes cooperative policies, whereas Bouncer defends against steered/drifting ones.

vs OOD / drift / concept-shift monitoring (hendrycks2017baseline, rabanser2019failing, gama2014survey, vovk2005algorithmic): those flag movement in the *input distribution*, which is mimickable - an adversary can keep covariate statistics in-distribution while degrading control. Bouncer instead measures *realized competence* (reward deficit) via secret dueling, and uses input-side tripwires only as a cheap Tier-A gate.

Mimicry resistance (Proposition) comes specifically from the *secrecy of the run-C/run-fallback set assignment*: an attacker cannot tell which accesses are being scored, so it cannot selectively perform well only on audited sets - a property absent from both deterministic set dueling and observable counter-based anomaly detectors.

Two-tier cost structure is novel for this problem: cheap always-on tripwires (covariate-shift sketch, confidence collapse, forward-model innovation) gate an expensive competence confirmer with a one-sided CUSUM (page1954cusum) sized via quickest-detection theory (lorden1971reacting, moustakides1986optimal) - giving near-minimal detection latency for competence regression under a bounded false-bounce budget, which prior systems guardrails (lo2015heracles, rzadca2020autopilot, carstens2023smartchoices) achieve only with bespoke, fault- or threshold-triggered logic per deployment.
